B.explanation: About $1330 \text{Hz}$ is the calculated frequency shift $f_s v_s/v$, which must be added to $122 \text{kHz}$.

C.explanation: A lower frequency than $122 \text{kHz}$ would mean a longer wavelength, which occurs when the source moves away, not towards.

D.explanation: The approaching source compresses the waves so $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s)$ gives about $123 \text{kHz}$.

Because the source moves towards the observer, successive $122 \text{kHz}$ wavefronts are crowded together so observed wavelength decreases and frequency increases.
Use $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ with $v_s = 16.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and check whether your result is slightly above $122 \text{kHz}$ in $\text{kHz}$, not in $\text{Hz}$.
walkthrough: Identify the Doppler situation: source speed $v_s = 16.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards stationary observer, source frequency $f_s = 122 \text{kHz}$, wave speed $v = 1480 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the rule for source approaching observer: observed wavelength is shortened, $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$, so observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ is greater than $f_s$.
Check sense and units: the increase is about $1.3 \text{kHz}$, consistent with $\Delta f \approx f_s v_s/v$, and the result stays in $\text{kHz}$. This is option D.
